protocol_type: EtherCAT runs three nested protocols in one packet: (a) the outer Ethernet frame (DA + SA + EtherType 0x88A4 + Payload + FCS), (b) the EtherCAT header (Length + Reserved + Type=0x1) selecting that the payload is an ESC-datagram block, (c) one or more EtherCAT datagrams chained by the Next bit, each carrying its own Cmd / Idx / Address / Length / IRQ / Data / Working Counter. A separate set of mailbox-resident application protocols (CoE / SoE / EoE / FoE / AoE / VoE) live on top of the SyncManager mailbox channels.

channels.name: Ethernet wire — Port 0 (Upstream)
channels.description: Standard 100BASE-TX or 100BASE-FX. Carries EtherType 0x88A4 frames (Raw mode) or UDP/IP encapsulated frames (UDP/IP mode, dst port 0x88A4).

channels.name: Ethernet wire — Port 1/2/3 (Downstream)
channels.description: Each downstream port forwards the in-flight frame to the next SubDevice while the on-the-fly engine reads/modifies/writes the addressed bytes. Last SubDevice's unused downstream ports loop the frame back upstream.

channels.name: PDI (Process Data Interface)
channels.description: Configurable: 8/16-bit asynchronous µC parallel bus, 8/16-bit synchronous µC parallel bus, SPI slave (mode 3 typically), Digital I/O (up to 32-bit out / 32-bit in), or on-chip CPU bus. Plus IRQ output, SYNC0/SYNC1 DC outputs, LATCH0/LATCH1 DC inputs.

channels.name: SII (EEPROM Slave Information Interface)
channels.description: I²C-compatible 2-wire (SCL, SDA) to a serial EEPROM (1 Kbit to 4 Mbit) holding the ESI descriptor. Default state is owned by ESC (PDI Access = 0); a request bit (ESC register 0x0501) hands ownership to the PDI.

packet_classes.purpose: Default low-latency on-segment transport. Destination MAC is unconstrained; SubDevices forward irrespective of DA.
packet_classes.format: Preamble (7B) + SFD (1B) + DA (6B) + SA (6B) + EtherType=0x88A4 (2B) + EtherCAT_Header (2B) + Datagram_block (variable, 60-1500B) + FCS (4B)

packet_classes.purpose: Cross-network routing through standard IP infrastructure (e.g., remote MainDevice over a routed network).
packet_classes.format: Eth(DA/SA/EtherType=0x0800) + IP (20-60B) + UDP (8B, dst=0x88A4) + EtherCAT_Header (2B) + Datagram_block + Eth_FCS (4B)

packet_classes.purpose: One unit of read/modify/write addressing carried inside the EtherCAT frame payload.
packet_classes.format: Cmd (1B) + Idx (1B) + Address (4B) + Length+Reserved+Circulating+Next (2B) + IRQ (2B) + Data (Length bytes) + Working_Counter (2B)

packet_classes.purpose: Carries application-protocol (CoE/SoE/EoE/FoE/AoE/VoE) messages between MainDevice and SubDevice via the canonical mailbox SyncManager pair.
packet_classes.format: Mbx_Header (6B: Length, Address, Channel+Priority, Type+Counter) + Mbx_Data (1-N B per protocol)

fields.name: Length
fields.description: Total length of all following datagrams in bytes.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: 0x1 = ESC datagram block (cyclic + acyclic). 0x4 = Network Variables (EAP). 0x5 = Mailbox-only.

fields.name: Idx
fields.description: MainDevice-local opaque datagram index, returned unchanged by SubDevices; used by the MainDevice to correlate response with request.

fields.name: Address
fields.description: Cmd-dependent: AP-cmd → Position(16b)+Offset(16b); FP-cmd → Configured_Station_Address(16b)+Offset(16b); BC-cmd → 0+Offset(16b); LRW/LRD/LWR → 32-bit Logical Address.

fields.name: Circulating
fields.description: Set if the datagram has already gone around the network once (Circulating frame).

fields.name: Next
fields.description: 1 = another datagram follows after this datagram's Data + WKC; 0 = this is the last datagram.

fields.name: IRQ
fields.description: Logical OR of AL Status interrupt requests collected from SubDevices that participated in the datagram.

datagram_tail.description: After the Data field, every datagram ends with a 16-bit Working Counter (WKC) updated by each addressed SubDevice.

commands_table.name: NOP
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: No SubDevice increments; WKC returns as transmitted (typically 0).

commands_table.name: APRD
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 by the SubDevice whose Position == 0 after increment.
commands_table.typical_use: Start-up sweep before SubDevices have a Configured Station Address.

commands_table.name: APWR
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 by the SubDevice whose Position == 0 after increment.

commands_table.name: APRW
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +3 by the SubDevice whose Position == 0 after increment (= +1 read + +2 write).

commands_table.name: FPRD
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 by every SubDevice whose Configured Station Address equals Address.
commands_table.typical_use: Targeted read of one specific SubDevice's register.

commands_table.name: FPWR
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 by every SubDevice whose Configured Station Address equals Address.
commands_table.typical_use: Targeted register write — AL Control, SM config, FMMU config.

commands_table.name: FPRW
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +3 by every SubDevice whose Configured Station Address equals Address.

commands_table.name: BRD
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 by every SubDevice; MainDevice observes total_slaves as the expected WKC.
commands_table.typical_use: Cyclic status sweep (e.g. read AL Status of every SubDevice in one datagram).

commands_table.name: BWR
commands_table.typical_use: Network-wide configuration (e.g. clear all ESC error counters with one datagram).

commands_table.name: LRD
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 by every SubDevice whose Read-Type FMMU maps the addressed bits.
commands_table.typical_use: Cyclic process-data INPUT (read sensors from many SubDevices in one datagram).

commands_table.name: LWR
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 by every SubDevice whose Write-Type FMMU maps the addressed bits.
commands_table.typical_use: Cyclic process-data OUTPUT (write actuators on many SubDevices in one datagram).

commands_table.name: LRW
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 for each successful read SubDevice, +2 for each successful write SubDevice (total = +3 per successful RW SubDevice).
commands_table.typical_use: Combined process-data IO in one datagram (most common cyclic command).

commands_table.name: ARMW
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 by the SubDevice whose Position == 0 after increment, which writes the data into the frame; every following SubDevice reads the data and copies it into its local memory.
commands_table.typical_use: Distributed Clock System Time propagation from the reference SubDevice to all DC SubDevices.

commands_table.name: FRMW
commands_table.wkc_increment_rule: +1 by the SubDevice whose Configured Station Address matches; every following SubDevice copies the data.
commands_table.typical_use: Re-distribute a value from one specific SubDevice (typically the DC reference) to all subsequent SubDevices in one frame.

addressing_modes.name: Position (AP)
addressing_modes.address_high_word_meaning: Signed 16-bit position; incremented by every SubDevice. Match when value == 0x0000.
addressing_modes.typical_use: Start-up enumeration before Configured Station Address has been written.

addressing_modes.name: Configured (FP)
addressing_modes.typical_use: Targeted access to one specific SubDevice after start-up.

addressing_modes.name: Broadcast (BC)
addressing_modes.typical_use: Network-wide status sweep or configuration write.

addressing_modes.name: Logical (LOG)
addressing_modes.address_high_word_meaning: Part of the 32-bit network-wide Logical Address space.
addressing_modes.low_word_meaning: Part of the 32-bit network-wide Logical Address space.
addressing_modes.typical_use: Cyclic process-data IO via FMMU mapping. One datagram can address up to 1486 B of logical space and many SubDevices.

esm_state_transitions.trigger: AL Control write = 0x02; SubDevice initialises mailbox SMs.
AL Control write = 0x03; SubDevice enters firmware-download mode.
AL Control write = 0x04; SubDevice activates process-data SMs and FMMUs, allows Inputs to update.
AL Control write = 0x08; SubDevice enables Output process-data driving local hardware.
AL Control write = 0x04 OR cyclic frame loss > SM watchdog → automatic.
AL Control write = 0x01 after firmware download.

mailbox_protocols_on_sm.name: CoE
mailbox_protocols_on_sm.description: SDO Read/Write, SDO Information, PDO transfer; full CiA 301/4xx Object Dictionary model. Most popular profile: DS-402 drive.

mailbox_protocols_on_sm.name: EoE
mailbox_protocols_on_sm.description: Tunnels arbitrary 802.3 Ethernet frames inside mailbox; for IP applications on the SubDevice.

mailbox_protocols_on_sm.name: FoE
mailbox_protocols_on_sm.description: TFTP-like WRQ/RRQ/DATA/ACK/ERROR; primarily for firmware download in Boot state.

mailbox_protocols_on_sm.name: SoE
mailbox_protocols_on_sm.description: Wraps Sercos III IDN-addressed parameter access.

mailbox_protocols_on_sm.name: AoE
mailbox_protocols_on_sm.description: Beckhoff's routed messaging protocol (AMS Net Id + Port).
